turns.text: ok the practical is a week from today and i need the skeleton part locked in. quiz me on bones and landmarks. short version of what to memorize first pls

Short version, the big ones:

1. Skull: frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital, sphenoid, ethmoid
2. Arm: humerus, radius (thumb side), ulna (pinky side)
3. Leg: femur, tibia (shin, big), fibula (skinny, outside)
4. Trunk: sternum, ribs, vertebrae, sacrum, coccyx
5. Landmarks: foramen magnum, mastoid process, olecranon, greater trochanter, medial malleolus

Ready? Q1: Which bone forms the back of the skull and has the foramen magnum?
occipital. ok next. im at the library btw gotta stand up every hour cuz my back stiffens when i sit lol

Correct. Standing breaks are a good idea, and this works fine on your feet.

Q2: Which forearm bone is on the thumb side?
radius. and the ulna has the olecranon right

Yes to both. The olecranon is the bony point of your elbow.

Q3: Which leg bone is the skinny one on the outside?
fibula. ok what's the medial malleolus i always blank on that one. dont give me a whole thing

The bump on the inside of your ankle. It's the end of the tibia. The outside bump is the lateral malleolus, on the fibula.

Q4: Which bone has the greater trochanter?
femur. i wanna find all of these on Gus at the tuesday group too. anything else to hit before then

Right. Before Tuesday, add these:

- Scapula: spine, acromion
- Clavicle: collarbone
- Pelvis: ilium, ischium, pubis
- Patella: kneecap
- Carpals and tarsals: wrist and ankle groups

On Gus, touch each bone and say its name and one landmark out loud. Last one: which bone is the shin?
Correct, 5 for 5 plus the extras. Review the add-on list a couple of times over the weekend and you'll be set.
